title: Automated detection and quantification of bone disorganization in hypophosphatasia before and after asfotase alfa: A case report

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Automated detection and quantification of bone disorganization in hypophosphatasia before and after asfotase alfa: A case report》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · p0035】In the present study, we investigated whether automated disorganization analysis could be applied to HPP, a disorder in which abnormal tissue organization is a fundamental pathological feature. Using plain distal radius radiographs obtained before and after six months of asfotase alfa therapy in a 16-year-old patient with severe HPP (Bowden and Adler, 2018), we evaluated the ability of ALIGNOGRAM to detect overt, subtle, and covert disorganized lesions and to quantify treatment-associated longitudinal changes in bone disorganization.

【Introduction · p0010】According to the prevailing view, healthy bone is characterised by adequate mineralized matrix reflected by normal bone mineral density (BMD), as well as preserved structural integrity, including normal cortical thickness and density and a well-connected trabecular architecture (Kanis, 2002; Zebaze et al., 2010). Although BMD and bone microarchitecture are important determinants of skeletal strength, they do not fully explain fracture susceptibility in many skeletal disorders (Zebaze and Ebeling, 2023; Zebaze et al., 2023). An additional determinant is how the components that make up bone are organized relative to one another. Bone quantity reflects how much bone material is present, structure describes its architecture, and organization describes how its components are arranged and integrated. Normal BMD or apparently preserved architecture does not necessarily produce strong bone if those components are poorly aligned or abnormally arranged. Bone disorganization refers to this loss of normal spatial organization (Zebaze and Ebeling, 2023; Zebaze et al., 2023).

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Automated detection and quantification of bone disorganization in hypophosphatasia before and after asfotase alfa: A case report》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Patient/images · p0040】Disorganization analysis was performed using ALIGNOGRAM 1.0 (Zebaze et al., 2023). Wrist radiographs from a 16-year-old male with severe childhood-onset HPP were analysed before and after six months of treatment with asfotase alfa (2 mg/kg administered subcutaneously three times weekly) (Bowden and Adler, 2018; Bowden and Foster, 2018). The radiographs were obtained from an open-access dataset available under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial (CC BY-NC) license (Bowden and Adler, 2018). Permission to reproduce the selected images was obtained from Dove Medical Press Ltd., and the study protocol was approved by the Monash Health Human Research Ethics Committee.

【Introduction · p0030】To address these limitations, we previously developed ALIGNOGRAM, an automated image-analysis platform that quantifies bone disorganization from conventional radiographs (Zebaze et al., 2023). In patients with atypical femoral fractures (AFFs), ALIGNOGRAM identified overt disorganized lesions and distinguished affected individuals from healthy controls. Importantly, it also detected subtle abnormalities within contralateral femora that appeared radiographically normal, distinguishing these femora from those of healthy controls (Zebaze et al., 2023). These findings are supported by the observation that up to 62.5% of AFFs are bilateral (Probyn et al., 2015), suggesting that structural abnormalities may exist before becoming visually apparent.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Automated detection and quantification of bone disorganization in hypophosphatasia before and after asfotase alfa: A case report》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Quantification of disorganization · p0065】The software then performs pixel-by-pixel analysis, quantifying local disorganization according to two key features: (i) spatial mislocation of a pixel relative to its neighbors and (ii) differences in normalized X-ray attenuation (greyscale intensity). These features are combined to generate a disorganization value (DV) for every pixel. The analysis is conducted on neighbouring pixels within a moving symmetric analysis window centered on each pixel of interest. The first layer includes the eight immediate neighbors in a 3 × 3 grid, while the second layer encompasses an additional sixteen next-nearest neighbors within a 5 × 5 window, totaling 24 surrounding pixels. By considering this extended neighborhood, the method captures more complex local patterns and enhances the sensitivity of disorganization detection. The analysis window moves across the image, analyzing successive pixels until the entire selected bone region has been covered.

【Quantification of disorganization · p0070】To identify disorganized pixels (i.e., local outliers), a threshold was applied to the matrix of 24 neighbouring pixels using the formula.where Q3 represents the third quartile and IQR the interquartile range of neighbouring DV values (Barbato et al., 2011). Pixels exceeding this critical disorganization value (CDV) were flagged as disorganized. The threshold was adopted unchanged from the previously published and validated ALIGNOGRAM methodology, which demonstrated that CDV tracked experimentally imposed disorganization and discriminated between clinical groups (Zebaze et al., 2023). It was not optimized for this case, and alternative thresholds were not tested; therefore, the sensitivity of the present findings to threshold choice remains unknown. This operational threshold identifies local outliers and should not be interpreted as an established biological or clinical cutoff in HPP. Connectivity analysis was then used to group adjacent disorganized pixels into distinct regions of abnormality, denoted as disorganized lesions.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Automated detection and quantification of bone disorganization in hypophosphatasia before and after asfotase alfa: A case report》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Fig. 1 · f0005】Fig. 1 Automated detection of an overt disorganized lesion with the corresponding quantitative disorganization profile.(A) Original distal radius radiograph showing the region of interest. The automatically detected lesion is outlined by the orange dashed rectangle.(B) ALIGNOGRAM split-screen display of the detected lesion. The left panel shows the lesion on the original radiograph, while the right panel presents the corresponding color-coded disorganization map. White arrows indicate the lesion location.(C) Corresponding ALIGNOGRAM disorganization profile. The lesion is associated with a focal increase in disorganization, appearing as a peak followed by a trough in the profile. Vertical dashed lines indicate the automatically identified lesion boundaries.

【Fig. 2 · f0010】Fig. 2 Automated detection of a subtle disorganized lesion with the corresponding quantitative disorganization profile.(A) Original distal radius radiograph showing the region of interest. The automatically detected lesion is outlined by the orange dashed rectangle. The lesion is inconspicuous on routine visual inspection.(B) ALIGNOGRAM split-screen display of the detected lesion. (B1) Original radiograph showing the automatically localized lesion. The right panel presents the corresponding color-coded disorganization map. White arrows indicate the lesion location. (B2) Magnified and contrast-enhanced view of the same region, demonstrating the subtle structural abnormality.(C) Corresponding ALIGNOGRAM disorganization profile. The lesion is associated with a focal increase in disorganization, producing a gradual peak within the profile. Vertical dashed lines indicate the automatically identified lesion boundaries.

【Fig. 3 · f0015】Fig. 3 Automated detection of a covert disorganized lesion with the corresponding quantitative disorganization profile.(A) Original distal radius radiograph showing the region of interest. The automatically detected lesion is outlined by the orange dashed rectangle. The abnormality was not identified on initial visual assessment.(B) ALIGNOGRAM split-screen display of the detected lesion. The left panel shows the automatically localized lesion on the original radiograph together with a magnified, contrast-enhanced view of the same region, in which the structural abnormality becomes apparent. The right panel presents the corresponding color-coded disorganization map. White arrows indicate the lesion location.(C) Corresponding ALIGNOGRAM disorganization profile. The lesion is associated with a focal increase in disorganization, characterised by a peak followed by a trough in the profile. Vertical dashed lines indicate the automatically identified lesion boundaries.
